manifest.title: Peergos
manifest.author: Peergos Developers
manifest.tagline: Private, end-to-end encrypted storage, sharing and social
manifest.description:
This is an unofficial community package. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Peergos or Cloudron. The packaging was written with the help of Claude, an AI model by Anthropic. Package source: [github.com/tripod0429/peergos-app](https://github.com/tripod0429/peergos-app).

### About

Peergos is a peer-to-peer, end-to-end encrypted global filesystem with fine-grained access control.

The server only ever sees encrypted data, and your identity is not tied to one server: you can log in through any Peergos instance and interact with users on other servers.

### Features

* File storage and sharing, with secret links
* Calendar
* Social feed
* Private websites
* Sandboxed third-party apps
manifest.postInstallMessage:
**Create the first account.** On first start Peergos prints a single-use signup link to the app logs. Look for the line containing `signup=true` and open it **without** the `:8000` that Peergos adds, i.e. `https://$CLOUDRON-APP-DOMAIN/?signup=true&token=...`. The first sync with the Peergos PKI can take a few minutes.

**Built-in apps need subdomains.** The PDF viewer, calendar, editor and other apps are served from subdomains of this app. Add the alias `*.$CLOUDRON-APP-DOMAIN` (needs a DNS provider Cloudron can drive, for the wildcard certificate). Without a wildcard, add `pdf`, `calendar`, `code-editor`, `markup-viewer`, `email` and `address-book` subdomains as aliases; third-party apps won't work then.

**Peer-to-peer ports.** Allow port 4001 over TCP and UDP in any firewall in front of the server.

**Settings** live in `/app/data/env.sh`. Edit it with the File Manager, then restart the app. Each setting is explained in the file; the most useful are `PEERGOS_ADMIN_USERNAMES` and `PEERGOS_DEFAULT_QUOTA` (1 GiB per user by default).
manifest.changelog:
* First published version, for Peergos 1.37.0
* Java now comes from Ubuntu's openjdk-25 package
* The logs warn when Peergos creates a database that backups don't handle yet
* Fixed the quota command in env.sh, which could leave files the app can't write
* App id is dev.tripod0429.peergos-app, to make clear this package is unofficial
* Logs only warnings and errors by default; set PEERGOS_LOG_LEVEL=INFO in env.sh for more

manifest.changelog:
* Update Peergos to 1.40.0 ([1.39.0](https://github.com/Peergos/web-ui/releases/tag/v1.39.0) and [1.40.0](https://github.com/Peergos/web-ui/releases/tag/v1.40.0) release notes), which includes security fixes for servers
* A restart during the very first start no longer leaves a server that can't start again
* A clone of the app, or a backup imported into a new app, no longer starts as a second copy of the same Peergos node until you confirm it (see Backup and restore in the README)
* The wildcard alias is required: the HTML viewer and third-party apps use hashed subdomains, so the docs no longer suggest individual aliases instead
